Looking at this problem, I need to find $f(n)$ for $n=1,\ldots,10$ and sum them.

## Setup

**Triconnected** means among any 3 vertices, at least 2 are connected. Equivalently, the complement graph $\bar{G}$ is **triangle-free** (no independent set of size 3 in $G$).

**Windmill with $n$ blades**: a center $O$ connected to $2n$ distinct vertices $A_1,B_1,\ldots,A_n,B_n$, with $A_iB_i$ an edge for each $i$. In $\bar{G}$-terms: $O$ is non-adjacent to all $2n$ vertices, and each pair $A_iB_i$ is a non-edge. This is a **matching of size $n$** in the complement of the induced subgraph of $\bar{G}$ on the non-neighbors of $O$.

## Key Lemma

**Lemma**: If $H$ is triangle-free on $m \geq 2n+1$ vertices, then $\bar{H}$ has a matching of size $n$.

*Proof*: If $\bar{H}$ has max matching $\leq n-1$, at most $2n-2$ vertices are matched, leaving $\geq m - 2n+2 \geq 3$ unmatched vertices. Unmatched vertices in a maximum matching form an independent set in $\bar{H}$, hence a clique in $H$. A clique of size $\geq 3$ contradicts triangle-freeness. $\square$

So if any vertex $O$ has $|S_O| \geq 2n+1$ non-neighbors in $\bar{G}$ (i.e., $\deg_{\bar{G}}(O) \leq N-2n-2$), a windmill exists.

## Upper Bound for $n \geq 2$: $f(n) \leq 4n+1$

Set $N = 4n+1$. For any triangle-free $\bar{G}$ on $N$ vertices:

**Case 1**: Some vertex has degree $\leq 2n-1$. Then $|S_O| \geq 4n+1-1-(2n-1) = 2n+1$. By the Lemma, a windmill exists.

**Case 2**: All vertices have degree $\geq 2n$. Since $2n > \frac{2(4n+1)}{5}$ for $n \geq 2$, the **Andrásfai–Erdős–Sós theorem** forces $\bar{G}$ to be bipartite with parts of size $2n$ and $2n+1$. Every vertex in the $(2n+1)$-part has degree exactly $2n$ (connected to all of the $2n$-part). Its $2n$ non-neighbors are the other vertices in the same part — an independent set in $\bar{G}$, so $\bar{H} = K_{2n}$, which has a perfect matching of size $n$. Windmill exists.

## Lower Bound for $n \geq 2$: $f(n) > 4n$

The complete bipartite graph $K_{2n,2n}$ on $4n$ vertices is triangle-free. Every vertex has degree $2n$, so $|S_O| = 2n-1 < 2n$. A matching of size $n$ requires $2n$ vertices, so **no windmill exists**. Thus $f(n) > 4n$.

Combining: $f(n) = 4n+1$ for $n \geq 2$.

## The Case $n = 1$: $f(1) = 6$

A windmill with 1 blade is a triangle. So $f(1) = R(3,3) = 6$ (every graph on 6 vertices contains a triangle or its complement does; triconnected forces the complement triangle-free, so $G$ has a triangle).

- **Lower bound**: $C_5$ on 5 vertices is triangle-free with $\bar{G} = C_5$, and $G = C_5$ has no triangle. Also $K_{2,2}$ on 4 vertices works. So $f(1) \geq 6$.
- **Upper bound**: $R(3,3) = 6$ gives $f(1) \leq 6$.

Note: $f(1) = 6 = 4(1)+2 \neq 4(1)+1 = 5$ because for $n=1$, AES doesn't apply ($2 \not> 2\cdot5/5$), and $C_5$ provides a non-bipartite counterexample on 5 vertices.

## Computation

$$f(1) = 6, \quad f(n) = 4n+1 \text{ for } n = 2,\ldots,10$$

$$f(2),\ldots,f(10) = 9, 13, 17, 21, 25, 29, 33, 37, 41$$

$$\sum_{n=1}^{10} f(n) = 6 + (9+13+17+21+25+29+33+37+41) = 6 + 225 = \boxed{231}$$
